messages:
maya: heads up — noticed a ton of noise in inspect sessions where redaction replaces multi-line user content with repeated `<REDACTED>` blocks. makes traces huge and useless for quick debugging :face_with_head_bandage:

sam: yeah i've seen that too. mostly from long user prompts or pasted logs. what are you thinking? :thinking:

maya: proposal: introduce a 'scrub-traceback' pass that collapses consecutive redacted ranges into a short summary token and attach a provenance hash + length. so instead of 30 lines of `<REDACTED>` we store `<REDACTED x3 blocks, 432 chars, h=sha256:abcd1234>`

jorge: sounds reasonable. concerns: does that break audit/legal requests? we need to ensure the provenance hash + length + route metadata is sufficient to rehydrate during a gated inspect flow (with TTL + audit log)

maya: rehydrate only allowed for tenant owners + ops with breakglass. rehydration would require key-unlock and an audit entry. normal console inspect shows summary token only.

tess: UI note — product wants an indicator in the console showing "collapsed for privacy" with hover to reveal metadata. also want a toggle (canary) for teams who enabled detailed inspect to see full redactions for initial rollout.

sam: quick sketch of compress logic:
```
def compress_redactions(ranges):
    merged = merge_adjacent(ranges)
    for r in merged:
        yield f"<REDACTED blocks={r.count} chars={r.total_len} h=sha256:{r.hash[:8]}>"
```
We keep indexes so rehydrate can map back to original blob stored in secure vault for TTL.

maya: performance: this adds a small pass in the scrubber (~1ms/msg) but reduces log size by 40-70% on heavy payloads. wins for quota/cost.

jorge: quota impact is huge — smaller logs reduce storage and transfer. but we must update sampling heuristics: if we collapse too aggressively, we might miss edge-case PII exposures during sampling. propose: keep original sampling signal from pre-compressed payload and attach sampling reasons to summary token.

tess: also need a UX decision for the inspect TTL: default 24 hours? legal asked for 7 days in some regions. suggest: platform default 24h, orgs can request extension with compliance justification.

maya: agree. default 24h. include an org-level config: inspect_ttl_days (1|7|30) but only available for private/dedicated customers via contract.

sam: one more thing — route-level opt-out. some noisy internal routes (metrics ingestion) should skip full scrub but still collapse repeated redaction blocks. add `scrub_profile: compact` vs `full`.

jorge: ops/breakglass flow: when rehydrating, we need an immutable audit event with who, why, and the original provenance hash must match. ops-bot should emit that.

ops-bot: note — we'll need to add an immutable entry in audit-log-stream and a k8s sidecar that enforces key access TTL and rotates rehydrate tokens every hour.

maya: rollout plan: 1) implement compress pass behind feature flag; 2) run for 10% of traces on hosted api (sampling keep original pre-compress signal); 3) expose console UI for collapsed tokens; 4) add rehydrate + audit for canary tenants; 5) iterate on TTL defaults.

sam: ACTION: i'll open a small RFC with pseudo-spec + benchmarks. assigning to @maya for scrub implementation and @jorge for audit/rehydration design.

maya: cool. who wants to volunteer for a quick PoC to measure latency?

jorge: i'll spin up a probe. will test with heavy prompt corpus and attachment payloads.

tess: UX follow-up: i'll mock the hover state and the inspect toggle — will drop prototypes in #design in 48h.

maya: thanks all. if anyone has regulatory concerns please ping legal-sync before we move beyond canary. :eyes:

sam: ack. will include compliance checklist in RFC. :+1:

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary feature flag created: scrub_traceback_compact_v1 — status: staged

maya: perfect. logging the thread and RFC link once opened.
